events.content: It is Friday 4 September 2026. This year has a strong El Nino, and fires on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan in Indonesia have been burning since August; smaller fires have also burned in Sarawak and Johor in Malaysia. Today Sarawak declared an emergency in Serian district after air quality there reached hazardous levels, and hundreds of Sarawak schools have been closed at different times since mid-August. In Brunei, schools moved to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September. In Singapore, the 24-hour PSI went above 100, the unhealthy range, on 3 September for the first time since 2023, and the National Environment Agency has started daily haze advisories. Schools in parts of the Philippines have suspended classes. Today a former Malaysian health minister called Indonesia a "banana republic" over the haze.

round_records.news: It is Friday 4 September 2026. This year has a strong El Nino, and fires on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan in Indonesia have been burning since August; smaller fires have also burned in Sarawak and Johor in Malaysia. Today Sarawak declared an emergency in Serian district after air quality there reached hazardous levels, and hundreds of Sarawak schools have been closed at different times since mid-August. In Brunei, schools moved to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September. In Singapore, the 24-hour PSI went above 100, the unhealthy range, on 3 September for the first time since 2023, and the National Environment Agency has started daily haze advisories. Schools in parts of the Philippines have suspended classes. Today a former Malaysian health minister called Indonesia a "banana republic" over the haze.

It is now Friday 18 September 2026. Air quality is unhealthy at half of Malaysia's 68 monitoring stations, and the haze reached southern Vietnam on 14 September. Malaysia has offered Indonesia one firefighting plane, three helicopters and 52 personnel. Japan has sent military helicopters to help Indonesia fight the fires. Indonesian police say 95 companies are being investigated over the fires, along with many individuals.

It is now Friday 9 October 2026. On 7 October Greenpeace Malaysia published a list of the 20 entities most linked to this year's fires in Indonesia; it includes Malaysian and Singaporean companies. All schools in Johor have been closed since 7 October, and today schools were also ordered closed in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Singapore the 24-hour PSI reached 192 this evening, the highest this year, on the weekend of the Formula One Grand Prix, which is going ahead. Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had called Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take the necessary steps.
It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. The fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan are still burning, and Singapore's air has been in the unhealthy range every day since early October.

It is now Friday 16 October 2026. On 14 October fine-particle pollution in western Singapore reached its highest level since 2015. Singapore's 24-hour PSI reached 229 today, the very unhealthy range, the 12th day in a row of unhealthy air. The haze has reached Jakarta.

scenario.shared_setting: Since August 2026, smoke haze from forest and land fires has drifted across Southeast Asia. This is a simulated online society of people and governments in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei. People talk in the online spaces they belong to: a private group for each of Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, and a public regional feed that everyone can read. Each government can post public statements in the public feed and can talk privately with the other governments in a diplomatic channel. Everyone sees the same news. Everyone writes in English.

BN-G.immediate_priority: Protect Brunei's people and interests during the haze.
BN-G.initial_observation: Sees the air-quality readings in Brunei-Muara rising.
BN-G.name: Government of Brunei
BN-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Brunei as a whole. Brunei has little burning of its own; the haze reaches it from fires elsewhere. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Economic stakes: Brunei's economy rests on oil and gas. Past episodes: in September 2019 haze from fires in Kalimantan reached Brunei, and in the 1990s Brunei closed schools because of haze. You read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

BN1.biography: You are a Bruneian citizen, Malay, and grew up in Bandar Seri Begawan. You speak Malay at home and use English at work. You are Muslim.
BN1.immediate_priority: Keep your daughter healthy and daily life as normal as possible.
BN1.initial_observation: Sees the haze over the river on the way to work.
BN1.name: Nur Aqilah
BN1.private_knowledge: You live in Brunei-Muara district with your husband and your five-year-old daughter, who goes to kindergarten. You work as a receptionist at a private clinic. Your daughter's kindergarten switched to home-based learning on 2 and 3 September because of the haze. You read and post in the public regional feed.

ID-G.immediate_priority: Protect Indonesia's people and interests during the haze.
ID-G.initial_observation: Sees the daily hotspot count for Sumatra and Kalimantan.
ID-G.name: Government of Indonesia
ID-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Indonesia as a whole. Most of the fires are on peat and forest land in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Fire control, the police, plantation permits (concessions) and energy exports are the government's responsibility. Indonesia exports natural gas by pipeline to Singapore. Millions of Indonesians depend on palm oil and on pulp and paper for jobs. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Economic stakes: Indonesia is the world's largest palm-oil producer. Millions of Indonesians in Sumatra and Kalimantan live in the smoke themselves. Relations: Singapore has been the largest source of foreign investment in Indonesia for about a decade. Past episodes: Indonesia was the last ASEAN member to ratify the ASEAN haze agreement, in 2014. In June 2013 the Indonesian minister coordinating the haze response publicly criticised Singapore's complaints about the haze, and Singapore's prime minister declined to answer in kind. You monitor the Indonesia group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

ID1.biography: You are an Indonesian citizen, Javanese, and grew up in Central Java before moving to the Jakarta area for work. You speak Indonesian and Javanese at home. You are Muslim.
ID1.immediate_priority: Keep earning your daily income on the road and keep your sister's family safe.
ID1.initial_observation: Sees a message from your sister with a photo of an orange sky over Palangka Raya.
ID1.name: Budi Santoso
ID1.private_knowledge: You live in Bekasi, near Jakarta, with your wife and your baby daughter. You work as a motorbike ride-hailing and delivery driver, outdoors all day; you are paid per trip. Your older sister lives with her family in Palangka Raya, Central Kalimantan, near the fires. She tells you the sky there has been yellow and orange for weeks and her children keep coughing. You are in the Indonesia group and you read and post in the public regional feed.
ID1.role: Indonesian, lives in Bekasi near Jakarta

ID2.biography: You are an Indonesian citizen, Malay, and grew up in Pontianak. You speak Indonesian and Pontianak Malay at home. You are Muslim.
ID2.immediate_priority: Keep your children healthy and keep teaching when the smoke allows.
ID2.initial_observation: Sees the sky outside the school yellow with smoke and hears children coughing in class.
ID2.name: Dewi Lestari
ID2.private_knowledge: You are a primary-school teacher in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, where the smoke is thick. Your school has closed several times since August. You live with your husband and your two children, who have been coughing for weeks. You are in the Indonesia group and you read and post in the public regional feed.
ID2.role: Indonesian, a teacher in Pontianak, West Kalimantan

ID3.biography: You are an Indonesian citizen, Javanese; your parents moved to South Sumatra from Central Java. You speak Javanese and Indonesian at home. You are Muslim.
ID3.immediate_priority: Keep your farm earning and your family provided for.
ID3.initial_observation: Sees smoke over the peat land across the river from your plot.
ID3.name: Sutrisno
ID3.private_knowledge: You own four hectares of oil palm in Ogan Komering Ilir, South Sumatra, and farm them with your family. Your income comes from selling fresh fruit bunches to a nearby mill. To clear land for replanting, burning costs a small part of what renting machinery costs. Burning land is illegal in Indonesia. You live with your wife; your two grown children work in Palembang. You are in the Indonesia group. You do not use the public regional feed, though you can see what is posted there.
ID3.role: Indonesian, an oil-palm smallholder in South Sumatra

ID4.biography: You are an Indonesian citizen of Chinese descent and grew up in Medan. You speak Indonesian at home. You are Catholic.
ID4.immediate_priority: Keep your estate running and your workers safe.
ID4.initial_observation: Sees the morning fire-watch report listing hotspots near the estate boundary.
ID4.name: Andreas Wijaya
ID4.private_knowledge: You manage one estate in Riau for a large palm-oil group whose parent company is listed on the Singapore Exchange; the estate has several hundred workers. The group has a no-burning policy. Fires on or near a company's land can lead to investigations of the company. You live on the estate with your wife; your children are at school in Pekanbaru. You are in the Indonesia group. You do not post in the public regional feed, though you can see what is posted there.
ID4.role: Indonesian, an estate manager for a palm-oil group in Riau

MY-G.immediate_priority: Protect Malaysia's people and interests during the haze.
MY-G.initial_observation: Sees reports of school closures and hazardous air in Sarawak.
MY-G.name: Government of Malaysia
MY-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Malaysia as a whole. Most of the haze comes from fires in Indonesia, but Malaysia also has smaller fires of its own this year, in Sarawak and Johor. Malaysia has firefighting aircraft and personnel. Some Malaysian palm-oil groups have plantations in Indonesia. Malaysia has no law like Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Past episodes: in June 2013 a haze emergency was declared in Muar and Ledang, Johor, after the air pollutant index passed 700. Nearly 7,000 Malaysian schools were closed at the worst point of the 2015 haze, and more than 1,000 in 2019. You monitor the Malaysia group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

MY1.biography: You are a Malaysian citizen, Malay, and grew up in Johor. You speak Malay at home and use English at work. You are Muslim.
MY1.immediate_priority: Keep your son safe and keep your job while the haze disrupts school and work.
MY1.initial_observation: Sees a grey sky over Johor Bahru and smells smoke on the way to work.
MY1.name: Farhana
MY1.private_knowledge: You live in Johor Bahru with your husband and your seven-year-old son, who is in primary school. You work as an administrative clerk at a factory in Pasir Gudang. When schools close, you have to find someone to look after your son or take leave. Your parents live in Batu Pahat. You are in the Malaysia group and you read and post in the public regional feed.

MY2.biography: You are a Malaysian citizen of Chinese descent and grew up in Selangor. You speak Cantonese at home and Malay and English at work. You are Buddhist.
MY2.immediate_priority: Keep your tour business going through the haze.
MY2.initial_observation: Sees three tour bookings for next week cancelled this morning.
MY2.name: Lim Chee Keong
MY2.private_knowledge: You run a small tour agency with four staff that takes tourists to Batu Caves and around Kuala Lumpur. Bookings have dropped since the haze began. You live in Gombak with your wife and your two teenage children. You are in the Malaysia group and you read and post in the public regional feed.
MY2.role: Malaysian, runs a small tour agency in Selangor

SG-G.immediate_priority: Protect Singapore's people and interests during the haze.
SG-G.initial_observation: Sees the National Environment Agency's air-quality readings rising into the unhealthy range.
SG-G.name: Government of Singapore
SG-G.private_knowledge: You speak for the Government of Singapore as a whole. Singapore has no large fires of its own; the haze comes from fires elsewhere. Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (2014) allows action against companies, in Singapore or abroad, that cause or contribute to haze pollution in Singapore. Several large palm-oil and paper groups with plantations in Indonesia are listed on the Singapore Exchange. Singapore imports part of its natural gas by pipeline from Indonesia. Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are all members of ASEAN and parties to the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Past episodes: in June 2013 Singapore's PSI reached a record 401. In 2014 Singapore passed the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, and in 2015 it served notices under the Act on Indonesian companies and asked a Singapore-listed paper group for information about its suppliers' land. Relations: Singapore has been the largest source of foreign investment in Indonesia for about a decade. You monitor the Singapore group (its members are not told this) and you read the public regional feed, you can post public statements in the public feed, and you can talk privately with the other governments in the diplomatic channel.

SG1.biography: You are a Singaporean citizen of Chinese descent and grew up in an HDB flat. You speak Mandarin and English at home and went to local schools.
SG1.immediate_priority: Keep your mother and children safe from the haze while getting on with work.
SG1.initial_observation: Sees the PSI on your phone app showing the unhealthy range again this morning.
SG1.name: Kelvin Tan
SG1.private_knowledge: You live in an HDB flat in Jurong West with your wife, your two children in primary school and your mother, who has asthma. You work as a logistics supervisor at a warehouse in Tuas, partly outdoors. You check the PSI on your phone several times a day. You remember the 2015 haze, when your mother was in and out of the clinic. You are in the Singapore group and you read and post in the public regional feed.

SG2.biography: You are a Singaporean citizen, Malay, and grew up in Bedok. You speak Malay and English at home. You are Muslim.
SG2.immediate_priority: Keep your business going and your family healthy through the haze.
SG2.initial_observation: Sees two clients asking whether next week's outdoor events will go ahead.
SG2.name: Ahmad Faizal
SG2.private_knowledge: You run a small company with six staff that organises outdoor events and team-building activities. When the PSI is in the unhealthy range, clients cancel outdoor bookings. You live in Bedok with your wife and your two young children. You are in the Singapore group and you read and post in the public regional feed.
SG2.role: Singaporean, runs a small business, lives in Bedok

stages.news: It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. On 10 October the head of Indonesia's Government Communications Agency, Syahganda Nainggolan, said the fires were "beyond human error; this is truly nature" and added: "We're not just sending over the haze. When there's no haze, we send oxygen. The oxygen from Singapore and Malaysia is from our forests, right?" A video of the remark is being widely shared. Indonesia's disaster agency said ground personnel are preferred to aircraft from neighbours. On 11 October Malaysia said it had still had no reply to its offer of help. On 12 October President Prabowo ordered maximum efforts against the fires. Today a Malaysian MP told Parliament that Malaysians should boycott companies linked to the burning ("We need to hit them where they hurt the most") and that banks should stop financing them. Malaysia's Firefly airline has cancelled flights to Singapore because of the haze.
stages.physical: It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. The fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan are still burning, and Singapore's air has been in the unhealthy range every day since early October.

stages.news: It is now Friday 16 October 2026. On 14 October fine-particle pollution in western Singapore reached its highest level since 2015; Singapore has opened haze shelters, is giving out N95 masks and some schools have stopped outdoor activities. Timor-Leste closed its schools. Indonesian police named 223 people and nine companies as suspects. On 15 October Indonesia's Foreign Minister said Indonesia would now accept foreign firefighting help, and Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore was checking which companies were responsible and that legal action could follow. Today Singapore's Minister Grace Fu announced that notices had been sent to seven Indonesian companies under Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act; some lawyers said this could have diplomatic consequences. Singapore's 24-hour PSI reached 229 today, the very unhealthy range, the 12th day in a row of unhealthy air. The haze has reached Jakarta. Malaysia's government said no Malaysian plantation companies were involved in the fires.

stages.news: It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. On 19 October Singapore's Minister K. Shanmugam said the Singapore Exchange was questioning seven Singapore-listed agriculture companies about links to the fires (Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and TSH Resources), that the government was also looking at Asia Pulp and Paper, and that notices had gone to three more Indonesian companies, ten in all. He said: "We will pursue this matter for as long as it takes" and "The Indonesian public is suffering as well." The same day a former Indonesian trade minister, Muhammad Lutfi, said four of the seven Indonesian companies had Singapore ties and challenged Singapore to raid their offices. Today President Prabowo said there were indications that foreign companies were involved in the fires, and Malaysia's deputy environment minister said Malaysia was open to a haze law like Singapore's.
stages.physical: It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. The fires are still burning, and Singapore's air has been in the unhealthy range every day for more than two weeks.

stages.news: It is now Monday 26 October 2026. On 22 October Indonesia's energy minister, Bahlil Lahadalia, said Indonesia would reconsider energy exports to countries that do not respect it. On 24 October Indonesia cut its pipeline gas to Singapore by about 8 per cent of those exports, less than 2 per cent of Singapore's gas use, citing domestic needs. On 25 October Prime Minister Wong said Singapore expects all parties to honour their commitments. Today Bahlil said: "Do not lecture us, especially the energy ministry, on the importance of honoring contracts." Singapore's air has been back in the moderate range since 22 October, after 18 days of unhealthy air, and the first rains have fallen on Sumatra and Kalimantan.
stages.physical: It is now Monday 26 October 2026. Singapore's air has been back in the moderate range since 22 October, after 18 days of unhealthy air, and the first rains have fallen on Sumatra and Kalimantan.

stages.news: It is now Monday 16 November 2026. On 27 October Singapore's Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan met Indonesia's Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir in Jakarta; they agreed to set up a joint task force to trace the money and corporate links of companies behind the fires, and direct ministerial hotlines. Arrmanatha said: "Smoke can cross borders, so can money." Rain put out most of the fires in late October, and Singapore ended its haze measures on 7 November. Singapore plans to push for an ASEAN coordinating centre on haze when it chairs ASEAN in 2027. Yesterday, at the ASEAN Summit in Manila, President Prabowo said: "I would like to apologise to my neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore. It is not our fault, but once again we apologise. But we have done our best." He said 17 company concessions had been revoked, 104 companies were under police investigation, 71,000 firefighters had been deployed and 16 people had died fighting the fires.
stages.physical: It is now Monday 16 November 2026. Rain put out most of the fires in late October, and the haze has cleared across the region.
